text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a consistent p99 jump during the 11:00 marketing bursts across two pods. p95 stable, p99 ~2.2x baseline for ~18s. KV cold-miss ratio spikes at the same time.

kai: ugh. is this scale-up lag or queueing backlog? can you paste the heatmap?

maria: dumping quick snippet from the profiler: 
```
p95: 120ms
p99: 640ms -> baseline 280ms
queue_depth_mean: 3.6 -> 12.4
kv_cold_miss_rate: 0.42 -> 0.82
microbatch_size_dist: mode=8, tail=32
```

devon: looks like two things colliding: (1) scale decision only sees average rps, so it reacts after the burst. (2) KV cache not prewarmed -> first few microbatches hit slow path and blow the p99.

anita: agree. we tried increasing microbatch to 32 to save cost but that worsens tail for short requests. p95 improves but p99 gets worse when KV cold misses combine with batching.

ryan: proposal: add a tiny probe stream and a signal smoother to the scaler. probe would be low-rate synthetic requests (no billing) tagged with `preheat` so runtime can prefill KV and stabilize kernel selection. smoother is a short EMA on p99 with alpha=0.3 to avoid flip-flopping on 10s spikes.

maria: sketch of autoscaler config I'd try: 
```
autoscaler:
  smoothing_window: 30s
  p99_ema_alpha: 0.3
  spike_detector:
    min_rps_for_spike: 4
    p99_multiplier_threshold: 1.4
  prober:
    enabled: true
    rate_per_pod: 0.1 # rps
    tag: preheat
```

kai: question: will probe requests skew cost metrics or user-visible quotas? we should mark them as internal so console filters them out. also ensure they use cached tokens so they don't go through heavy model branches.

devon: implementation notes from runtime side: probers should be scheduled with lower priority, go through a fast path kernel (fp16 int8) and only touch KV prefix-length=16 to prewarm caches. also add a new metric `kv_prefill_hits` so we can correlate.

anita: small experiment idea: run A/B for one hour during next expected burst window. A: current autoscaler. B: autoscaler+prober+smoother. Track p95/p99, cold_miss_rate, scale_events, cost_delta.

ryan: I'll wire prober flag as an opt-in feature for Dedicated clusters first. devon can add the metric to the runtime trace. can we also add a microbatch fallback heuristic: if current queue_depth > 8 and kv_cold_miss_rate > 0.3, temporarily force microbatch_mode=small (8->4) to reduce contention?

devon: yeah we can add a short-lived override for microbatch sizing (ttl=45s). but need to be careful with throughput loss. will simulate with the perf harness.

maria: plan sounds good. next steps: ryann (typo: ryan), can you schedule the A/B and toggle for next Tue 11:00? devon add metrics and sim, anita own analysis. I'll monitor live and abort if p99 gets worse. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for `prober-feature` to 2 pods at 2026-03-24T18:12:00Z

kai: nice. if this reduces cold-tail we might incorporate prober as a default opt-in for Hosted low-latency tiers.

maria: thanks all — keeping notes in the perf board. short follow-up: if probe causes more pressure on kernel selection (extra microbatches), we can throttle probe rate or target only a subset of pods.

anita: added experiment checklist to the perf board: heatmap baseline, probe on/off, kv_prefill_hits, p99_ema, cost.

ryan: scheduled. I'll also add console filter to hide probe traffic from customer billing view.

maria: closing loop — we'll reconvene after the run and decide next steps. :eyes:
